small_guidance:
- Add the softmax BLOCK_N (try 1024/2048/4096) and num_warps (4/8/16) to a `triton.autotune` over the softmax kernel keyed on N; with N=8192 a single-pass kernel using BLOCK_N=8192 and num_warps=16 may beat the 2-pass variant by halving DRAM traffic on out_gelu.
- Extend GEMM autotune with BLOCK_K=128 and num_stages=4 entries (e.g. 128x128x128, 64x256x64) — K=8192 is large and deeper pipelining typically helps on RTX 4090; also consider adding `num_warps=8` variants of the 128x128 tiles.
- Pre-transpose `W` once in `__init__` (store W^T contiguous as (in, out)) so the B operand has stride_bk=1 on the contiguous axis; this removes the strided B load from the hot loop.
large_guidance:
- Fuse the row-max and row-sum-exp of softmax into the GEMM epilogue: each program computing a (BLOCK_M, N_full) row tile can run a persistent N-loop accumulating max and ∑exp on the fly (online softmax) and write normalized outputs in a second N-pass — eliminates the full out_gelu materialization (M*N=8M floats of HBM round-trip).
- Alternative: split-K GEMM with atomic-free row partials, then a fused softmax-normalize kernel that reads partial tiles directly; shapes here (M=1024, N=K=8192) are well-suited to persistent split-K with one CTA per row group.
- If keeping the 2-kernel split, make the softmax kernel persistent (one program per SM looping over multiple rows) and use vectorized 4-wide loads to better hide latency on the 8192-wide rows.
